scope: Transaction and realtime ownership for one coordinated capability/hexagonal refactor; research only

recommendation.persistence: Keep specialized atomic workflow ports as the intended final design for current registration, message acceptance and gift purchase; one SQLite adapter may implement several small contracts with one generated sqlc package. Introduce explicit transaction scopes only for a concrete orchestration need that cannot be expressed cleanly as one workflow operation.
recommendation.realtime: Create a focused realtime/session state owner with typed inbound/outbound contracts; remove unrelated business rules and rendering from it. One shared state owner is a deliberate concurrency boundary, not a reason to retain the all-feature Application.
recommendation.delivery: A complete migration can be delivered as one coordinated change with internal dependency-ordered compilation and behavioral checkpoints. Splitting the user-facing delivery into multiple approvals is not required by these patterns.

current_invariants.post_commit: Cache the returned committed identity directly; do not reread through a possibly canceled request context.
Notify delivery using the committed message/outbox state; notification failure must not erase accepted work.

atomic_parts: Group membership or room mute checks
current_invariants.qualification: Live room membership/recipient snapshot comes from the application state owner; durable checks remain inside the same database transaction.
Preserve the existing responseGate -> deliveryGate -> state-lock order. No caller may wait for an outer gate while holding the state lock.

ordering: Mark durable delivery only after successful write
Release reservation after failure/cancellation for same-session retry
current_invariants.qualification: Current correlation uses *protocol.Packet keys. A typed event migration needs stable delivery handles so encoding or copying DTOs cannot lose completion correlation; native delivery remains at-least-once, not exactly-once.

options.name: Specialized atomic workflow port
options.example: accounts.RegistrationStore.Register(ctx, command) (Account, error); commerce.GiftStore.Purchase(ctx, command) (Receipt, error); chat.MessageStore.Accept(ctx, command) (Message, error)
options.benefit: Expresses the observable business transaction as one contract and keeps sqlc/database mechanisms in the adapter. Several logical capabilities can participate in one durable workflow without independently committing.
options.cost: Adapter must implement the whole persistence operation. Pure business calculations should live in capability policy code; current-state integrity checks need transactional reads/rechecks.
options.fit: Recommended for the current concrete workflows; valid final architecture, not a temporary escape hatch.

options.name: Explicit workflow transaction scope
options.example: WithinGift(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context, GiftLedger, GiftInventory, GiftMessages) error) error
options.benefit: Lets application orchestration combine named consumer-owned repository capabilities while adapter binds all implementations to one transaction.
options.cost: More contracts, callback scope/lifetime rules, and testing. Never retain scoped repositories, start nested transactions, or perform network I/O inside the callback. With the current one-connection pool, accidental nested repository transactions can deadlock.
options.fit: Optional for workflows whose application orchestration genuinely needs independent capabilities. This explicit transaction runner is not automatically Fowler's full object-change-tracking Unit of Work pattern.

options.name: Independent commits plus generic in-memory event bus
options.example: Commit purchase, publish GiftPurchased, another handler writes message
options.benefit: Loose call-site coupling for optional transient notifications.
options.cost: Breaks current atomicity when the process fails between commit and handling; adds ordering, retry and error-policy ambiguity.
options.fit: Do not replace required registration/gift/message/block invariants with it.

options.name: Durable outbox and asynchronous integration
options.example: Commit state plus event/outbox row, then owned worker delivers/retries
options.benefit: Appropriate for genuinely asynchronous effects and external provider integration.
options.cost: Requires persistence, ownership, ordering/idempotency policy and acceptance tests. Changes synchronous behavior if used indiscriminately.
options.fit: Existing message/audience pending records already provide durable delivery intent. Extend deliberately when actual provider/event requirements emerge; no generic bus is required for this refactor.

full_target_ownership: Accounts owns credentials, registration/recovery policy and committed account cache; expose immutable account views and a session-revocation collaborator port.

Realtime owns session state, presence, response/write gates, delivery reservations and live participation coordination. Keys are stable user/session IDs, not mutable account objects shared across modules.
Chat owns message/group policy and typed message use cases; persistence uses the atomic message port and realtime coordination for live room eligibility/snapshots.

Contacts owns roster/block policy; an explicit block workflow coordinates the realtime delivery fence, persistence commit, and queue invalidation. Use injected narrow interfaces rather than reciprocal concrete imports.
Commerce owns pricing/purchase policy and its specialized atomic purchase port; SQLite may write ledger, inventory and chat persistence within that one operation.
Native/HTTP compatibility adapters own opcodes, packet fields, HTML/templ projection and historical command quirks. Application capabilities expose typed commands/results/events.
Composition wires concrete services, adapters and collaborators once. No module imports cmd/internal wiring; bootstrap remains generic lifecycle only.
single_delivery_completion_criteria: Every chosen capability has an explicit owning service, narrow dependencies and semantic commands/results; no new method delegates back into a retained all-feature Application for its real business work.
Old broad repository/service aggregates are removed from final business constructors or limited to a composition-only compatibility bridge that carries no business state/rules.
One intentional realtime state owner remains; this is not duplicated across HTTP/socket/modules.
Cross-capability persistence operations retain current atomicity with one BeginTx per workflow and context-aware generated queries.
No business package imports protocol, templ/pages, net/http, database/sql, generated httpapi/sqlc or concrete adapters.
MessageInput canonical serialization/hash order and historical endpoint/opcode behavior are preserved or mapped through an explicit compatibility representation.
Existing rollback, successful-commit cancellation, credential-cache, block/write ordering, failed-delivery retry, vote/catalog cancellation and original-JAR suites pass against the final graph.

sources.supports: Related changes must share a transaction; mixing DB calls outside the active transaction can cause inconsistency or deadlock.
Generated Queries can bind to a transaction through WithTx/DBTX. Keep this project's explicit BeginTx(ctx,nil) convention rather than copying the context-free Begin example.
Adapters translate technology-specific interaction into semantic application ports; application behavior can be driven and tested without its runtime devices/database.
Unit of Work coordinates object changes and concurrency for a business transaction; a callback transaction runner alone does not implement every aspect of that pattern.
Persist state and delivery intent together to avoid dual-write gaps; asynchronous consumers need duplicate/ordering/retry policy. No AWS service adoption is implied.
